Subsequently, the Petitioner _36. In our view, the dispute raised falls within the jurisdiction of the Gujarat Commission before whom a petition already filed by the petitioner is pending.”_ - _(g) Pass such further order(s) as deemed appropriate in the facts of the case.”_ 12. The matter was called out for virtual hearing on 26.5.2022. During the course of hearing, learned senior counsel for the Petitioner referred the Petition and reiterated the submissions already captured in hereinabove. Whereas, learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of the Respondent No.1, made the following submissions: (c) The Respondent No. 1 had also approached this Commission in Petition No. 216/MP/2015 in regard to levy of CSS on the Respondent No.1 wherein the Commission vide its order dated 6.7.2016 observed that the dispute raised by the Respondent No.1 falls within the jurisdiction of GERC. 13. In rebuttal, learned senior counsel for the Petitioner referred to the Commission's order dated 6.11.2018 in Petition No. 151/MP/2016 and submitted that the similar objections raised by the Respondent No.1 had already been rejected by this Commission therein. Learned senior counsel further submitted that the present Petition does not only seek invocation of Section 142 of the Act but also the recall of appropriate forum to decide the same [Para 36 of order dated 6.7.2017 in Petition No. 216/MP/2015]. The present Petition, therefore, is a clear case of misuse of process and is not only premature but also not maintainable at this stage when the issue concerning the liability to pay CSS is yet to be determined by GERC. Judicial propriety also demands that this Commission awaits the outcome of the GERC proceedings. (f) There is also a likelihood of conflicting decisions by two regulatory commissions on the very same issue. In the event this Commission were to allow the present Petition and GERC were to hold that the Respondent is not liable to pay CSS, the same would amount to conflicting decisions on the very same issue between the very same parties, an outcome which must be avoided. Therefore, on this score as well, judicial propriety requires that this Commission declines to entertain the present Petition in its present form. (g) Without prejudice to the above, the observations of the Commission in its order dated 6.11.2018 to the effect that the Respondent is liable to pay CSS and on which much reliance is being placed by the Petitioner, in addition to the being obiter observations, are also under challenge before the APTEL in Appeal No.13 of 2021, which stands admitted. It is settled law that once an appeal is admitted by an appellate court, the sub-ordinate court must ordinarily not seek compliance of their order impugned before the Appellate court. Therefore, this Commission must exercise judicial restraint in entertaining this Petition. (j) In the event the Petitioner agrees upon the aforesaid conditions, the Commission may dispose of the present Petition in terms of the same without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case. 17. We have considered the submissions made by the Petitioner and the Respondent No.1. At this stage, the limited question before us is as to whether the present Petition is maintainable or not. 20. We have considered the submissions made by the parties. As rightly pointed out by the Petitioner, the issue as to whether the present Petition is maintainable in view of the pendency of the Petitions before the GERC is squarely covered by the decision of this Commission dated 6.11.2018 in Petition No. 151/MP/2016, which was filed by the Petitioner on the identical subject matter. In the said order, while dealing with the objection of the Respondent No.1 regarding non-maintainability of the Petition on the basis of the pendency of the Petitions before the GERC with regard to CSS, the Commission observed as under: ## **_Issue No.1: Whether the Petition is maintainable before the Commission in view of the (i) pendency of the Petitions before GERC with regard to Cross Subsidy Surcharge, and (ii) commencement of the Insolvency Proceedings before National Company Law Tribunal?_** _The Commission in para 49(j) of the order dated 8.6.2013 in Petition No.245/MP/2012 issued the following directions:_ _32. Since there is moratorium on continuation of pending suits or proceedings during the pendency of the matter before NCLT under section 14(1)(a) of IBC, we are constrained to issue any directions on the prayers of the Petitioner. However, under Section 60(5) of the IBC, a corporate person can approach NCLT for appropriate directions. Section 60(5) of the IBC is relevant which is extracted as under:_ 22. The Respondent No.1 has submitted that the order dated 6.11.2018 in Petition No. 151/MP2016 is, however, under challenge before the APTEL in Appeal No. 13 of 2021, which is admitted by APTEL and thus, the Commission ought not to proceed for 23. In view of the foregoing observations and discussions, we hold that the present Petition is maintainable. Accordingly, the notice is issued to the parties and the Respondents are directed to file their reply on merits within four weeks after serving copy to the Petitioner who may file its rejoinder, if any, within three weeks thereafter.
